newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf unit unions call June 5 strike day.
newsitem.headline: Elf unit unions call June 5 strike day.

text.p: Five labour unions at the chemicals unit of French oil giant Elf Aquitaine called for a day of strike on June 5 to press for working time reduction instead of lay-offs.

The strike call, which follows a stand-off between management and unions since April 24, will be a first test of resolve for the new left-wing government which in general supports working time reduction as a way to create jobs.

The strike at Elf Atochem, where 1,000 jobs stand to diappear between now and the year 2000, comes on top of restructuring at carmaker Renault and the planned closure of its Vilvoorde plant in Belgium, as well as plans by other carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen to shed 2,816 jobs.

In a joint statement, the five unions at Elf Aquitaine's Atochem said that: "Faced with the refusal of the general management, the five unions CGT, CFDT, CFTC, FO and CGC call upon the staff of the 23 sites of Elf Atochem to show a powerful movement of unified and coordinated action."

"The unions CGT, CFDT, CFTC and FO call for a 24-hours strike day with a halt of production on Thursday June 5, 1997. The CGC associates itself to that day with another form of action than a strike," the statement said.
On June 6, the unions are set to meet to discuss the outcome of the strike and demand that negotiations be re-opened.
Elf Atochem chairman Jean Puechal told unions in December that the group planned an annual job reduction of two percent up to the year 2000. The unions said this concerned 1,000 jobs.
They said they wanted "the creation of jobs by all forms of massive and diversified working time reduction with the keeping of pay."

The unions proposed a 35 hour working week for staff on day and semi-continuous shifts and 33 hours 36 minutes for people working on continuous shifts. They also asked for early retirement at 55 years for some of the staff.
